title: Site comparison reflects finite-Tor constructibility of bounded-below inputs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and the exact comparison pullback $
u_T^*$ for $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $C\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be any bounded-below complex, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Suppose that $
u_T^*C$ is bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: its derived tensor with every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf has cohomology only in that interval [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then $C$ is bounded with constructible etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $C$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $C\otimes_A^L N$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf $N$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-kun-derived-tensor]. No constructibility hypothesis on $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), together with the bounded-below fully faithful comparison and the finite-Tor comparison of the blueprint. Agent-explicit reflection consequence for arbitrary bounded-below inputs, not a verbatim statement of Tag 09AK.

proof.text: Write $F=\nu_T^*$. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], on ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves $F$ is exact and fully faithful; this applies to our discrete commutative ring $A$. Its derived functor is the termwise functor specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For any representing complex $P$, exactness identifies $\ker F(d^i)$ with $F(\ker d^i)$ and $\operatorname{im}F(d^{i-1})$ with $F(\operatorname{im}d^{i-1})$, and preserves their quotient. Hence $H^i(FP)\cong F(H^iP)$, and therefore $H^i(FC)\cong F(H^iC)$. Also, if $FM=0$, then $F(1_M)=0=F(0)$, so faithfulness gives $1_M=0$ and $M=0$. Thus $F$ reflects zero module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 099T, lemma-fully-faithful; cohomology calculation from exactness, as in Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible

proof.text: By the boundedness hypothesis there are integers $u\le v$ such that $H^i(FC)=0$ outside $[u,v]$. Step 1 gives $F(H^iC)=0$ there and hence $H^iC=0$. Thus $C$ is bounded in the same cohomological interval. This argument also covers $FC=0$: choose any finite interval and conclude that every cohomology sheaf of $C$ vanishes.

source.place: Tag 099T, lemma-fully-faithful; elementary reflection of cohomological vanishing

proof.text: For each integer $i$, the sheaf $H^i(FC)$ is intrinsically constructible by hypothesis. Apply the sheaf equivalence, clause (i) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], at the given finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$. It supplies a constructible etale sheaf $G_i$ and an isomorphism $FG_i\cong H^i(FC)\cong F(H^iC)$. Fullness on all module sheaves in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to maps $G_i\to H^iC$ and $H^iC\to G_i$. Faithfulness makes both composites identities, so $H^iC\cong G_i$. Transporting the finite stratification and the local constant finite-module models along this isomorphism shows that $H^iC$ is constructible. Together with step 2 this is exactly the bounded constructible condition of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. No constructibility of $C$ was used to obtain $G_i$.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, sheaf equivalence; reflection through the fully faithful functor of lemma-fully-faithful

proof.text: Apply clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] with $K=FC$, the etale antecedent $C$, and the identity isomorphism $K\cong\nu_T^*C$. Its hypotheses hold: $A$ is the specified finite coefficient stage, $C$ is bounded below by the original hypothesis, and $K$ is intrinsically bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in the given interval $[a,b]$. Moreover $\ell$ is invertible on $T$: since $k$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$, the image of $\ell$ has an inverse in $k$, and its image under the structure map remains an inverse on every open of $T$. The cited clause gives etale Tor amplitude in this same interval, for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf. Together with step 3 this proves both conclusions.
